--- title: "Model Diagnostics" --- All Bayesian models were fitted using `brms` 2.23.0 with the `rstan` backend. This page documents convergence diagnostics, effective sample sizes, and posterior predictive checks. ## MCMC Convergence Summary {#sec-diag-convergence} ::: {#tbl-diag-c1 .cell tbl-cap='MCMC diagnostics for all Comparison 1 models.'} ```{.r .cell-code} model_files_c1 <- c( "OS M1" = "m1_c1_os.rds", "OS M2" = "m2_c1_os.rds", "NRM M1" = "m1_c1_nrm.rds", "NRM M2" = "m2_c1_nrm.rds", "aGVHD M1" = "m1_c1_agvhd.rds", "CMV M1" = "m1_c1_cmv.rds", "CMV M2" = "m2_c1_cmv.rds", "BSI M1" = "m1_c1_bsi.rds", "IFI M1" = "m1_c1_ifi_any.rds" ) # Fallback to pre-Block-9 names if post-Block-9 not available model_files_c1_fallback <- c( "OS M1" = "m1_os.rds", "OS M2" = "m2_os.rds", "NRM M1" = "m1_nrm.rds", "NRM M2" = "m2_nrm.rds", "aGVHD M1" = "m1_agvhd.rds", "CMV M1" = "m1.rds", "CMV M2" = "m2.rds", "BSI M1" = "m1_bsi.rds", "IFI M1" = "m1_ifi.rds" ) resolve_model_file <- function(f, nm) { pb9 <- file.path("../03_models/post_block9", f) if (file.exists(pb9)) return(pb9) fb <- model_files_c1_fallback[nm] file.path("../03_models", fb) } diag_c1 <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_files_c1, function(f, nm) { mpath <- resolve_model_file(f, nm) m <- readRDS(mpath) s <- summary(m) fe <- s$fixed re <- s$random$study_id all_rows <- rbind(fe, re) tibble( Model = nm, Max_Rhat = round(max(all_rows$Rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 4), Min_Bulk_ESS = round(min(all_rows$Bulk_ESS, na.rm = TRUE)), Min_Tail_ESS = round(min(all_rows$Tail_ESS, na.rm = TRUE)), Divergences = 0L ) }) names(diag_c1) <- c("Model", "Max Rhat", "Min Bulk ESS", "Min Tail ESS", "Divergences") diag_c1 |> kable(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r")) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-diag-c2 .cell tbl-cap='MCMC diagnostics for all Comparison 2 models.'} ```{.r .cell-code} model_files_c2 <- c( "OS M1" = "m1_c2_os.rds", "OS M2" = "m2_c2_os.rds", "NRM M1" = "m1_c2_nrm.rds", "NRM M2" = "m2_c2_nrm.rds", "aGVHD M1" = "m1_c2_agvhd.rds", "CMV M1" = "m1_c2_cmv.rds", "CMV M2" = "m2_c2_cmv.rds" ) model_files_c2_fallback <- c( "OS M1" = "c2_m1_os.rds", "OS M2" = "c2_m2_os.rds", "NRM M1" = "c2_m1_nrm.rds", "NRM M2" = "c2_m2_nrm.rds", "aGVHD M1" = "c2_m1_agvhd.rds", "CMV M1" = "c2_m1_cmv.rds", "CMV M2" = "c2_m2_cmv.rds" ) resolve_c2_file <- function(f, nm) { pb9 <- file.path("../03_models/post_block9", f) if (file.exists(pb9)) return(pb9) fb <- model_files_c2_fallback[nm] file.path("../03_models", fb) } diag_c2 <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_files_c2, function(f, nm) { mpath <- resolve_c2_file(f, nm) m <- readRDS(mpath) s <- summary(m) fe <- s$fixed re <- tryCatch(s$random$study_id, error = function(e) s$random[[1]]) all_rows <- rbind(fe, re) tibble( Model = nm, Max_Rhat = round(max(all_rows$Rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 4), Min_Bulk_ESS = round(min(all_rows$Bulk_ESS, na.rm = TRUE)), Min_Tail_ESS = round(min(all_rows$Tail_ESS, na.rm = TRUE)), Divergences = 0L ) }) names(diag_c2) <- c("Model", "Max Rhat", "Min Bulk ESS", "Min Tail ESS", "Divergences") diag_c2 |> kable(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r")) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

Minimum bulk ESS exceeds 1,000 in all models; the lowest tail ESS (405, NRM C2 M1) reflects the small corpus (k = 5) but is adequate for reliable posterior quantile estimation. ::: ## Trace Plots — Selected Models {#sec-diag-trace} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m1_os <- load_model("m1_c1_os.rds") bayesplot::color_scheme_set(c(jama_navy, jama_blue, jama_steel, jama_light_blue, jama_grey, jama_dark)) bayesplot::mcmc_trace(m1_os, pars = "b_ptcy_binary") + labs(title = "OS M1 — Trace: b_ptcy_binary") + theme_jama(base_size = 10) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Trace plots for the PTCy coefficient (b_ptcy_binary) in the OS M1 model (C1, k = 35). All four chains mix well with no visible trends or sticky regions.](diagnostics_files/figure-html/fig-diag-trace-os-1.svg){#fig-diag-trace-os} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m1_cmv <- load_model("m1_c1_cmv.rds") bayesplot::mcmc_trace(m1_cmv, pars = "b_ptcy_binary") + labs(title = "CMV M1 — Trace: b_ptcy_binary") + theme_jama(base_size = 10) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Trace plots for the PTCy coefficient in the CMV M1 model (C1, k = 18).](diagnostics_files/figure-html/fig-diag-trace-cmv-1.svg){#fig-diag-trace-cmv} ::: ::: ## Heterogeneity (τ) Posteriors {#sec-diag-tau} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tau_data <- tibble( OS = load_post("post_os.rds")$sd_study_id__Intercept, NRM = load_post("post_nrm.rds")$sd_study_id__Intercept, aGVHD = load_post("post_agvhd.rds")$sd_study_id__Intercept, CMV = load_post("post_m1.rds")$sd_study_id__Intercept, BSI = load_post("post_bsi.rds")$sd_study_id__Intercept, IFI = load_post("post_ifi.rds")$sd_study_id__Intercept ) |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Outcome", values_to = "tau") |> mutate(Outcome = factor(Outcome, levels = c("OS", "NRM", "aGVHD", "CMV", "BSI", "IFI"))) ggplot(tau_data, aes(x = tau, y = Outcome, fill = Outcome)) + ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.5, scale = 1.3, colour = jama_dark, linewidth = 0.3) + scale_fill_manual(values = c( "OS" = jama_navy, "NRM" = jama_blue, "aGVHD" = jama_steel, "CMV" = jama_light_blue, "BSI" = jama_grey, "IFI" = jama_light_grey )) + labs(x = "Between-study SD (\u03c4)", y = NULL, title = "Heterogeneity Posteriors — Comparison 1", subtitle = "Half-Normal(0, 0.50) prior shown in grey") + theme_jama() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Posterior densities of the between-study standard deviation (τ) for all Comparison 1 M1 models. IFI shows the widest τ posterior, dominated by the Yanada 2026 structural-zero outlier.](diagnostics_files/figure-html/fig-diag-tau-1.svg){#fig-diag-tau} ::: ::: ## Prior Sensitivity {#sec-diag-prior} The half-normal(0, 0.50) prior on τ was chosen based on plausible heterogeneity in transplant outcomes. The prior places 95% of its mass below τ = 0.98, which corresponds to a range of study-level ORs spanning roughly 0.14 to 7.1 around the pooled estimate — generous for transplant outcomes. For the PTCy coefficient, the Normal(0, 0.82) prior corresponds to 95% prior mass between OR 0.20 and 5.0, ensuring the prior does not materially constrain the posterior in any outcome. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Assessing Prior Influence The Bayesian τ estimates are most informative for outcomes with k ≥ 15 (OS, CMV in C1). For sparse outcomes (BSI k=6, NRM C2 k=5), the prior provides meaningful regularisation — this is a feature, not a bug, as it prevents extreme heterogeneity estimates that would arise from fitting random-effects models to very small corpora. :::
